hypotheses.justification: Continuity of F supplies the local bound needed by dominated convergence. At each t₀, IsCompact.exists_bound_of_continuousOn bounds ‖F‖ on [t₀ - 1 - T, t₀ + 1]; enlarge this bound to a nonnegative D. For |t - t₀| < 1 and 0 < τ ≤ T, this bounds ‖F (t - τ)‖. Repeat the existing continuousAt proof with D replacing C and this neighborhood bound replacing hFC: intervalIntegral.continuousAt_of_dominated_interval requires domination only eventually near t₀. The existing integrable Abel kernel and almost-everywhere continuity arguments remain unchanged. T = 0 gives a zero integral.
It follows from hFC at time zero: (norm_nonneg (F 0)).trans (hFC 0). Supply this proof to mildShiftedStokesIntegral_continuousAt instead of hC. This also covers C = 0.

Split on 0 ≤ T. The nonnegative case uses the existing proof. Otherwise T < 0, and every τ in the unordered interval between 0 and T satisfies τ ≤ 0. By its definition, mildShiftedStokesIntegrand is therefore zero throughout that interval, for every t. intervalIntegral.integral_congr and intervalIntegral.integral_zero make the integral identically zero, hence continuous. T = 0 is already covered.
